posts.text:
Today on Social Media Harms Victim Remembrance Day, we honor those we've lost and the families advocating for change.

I worked to pass the TAKE IT DOWN Act to combat AI-generated deepfakes, and I'll keep fighting for stronger protections for children and greater accountability for social media companies.

The most significant federal housing bill in 30 years has passed out of Congress — the bipartisan ROAD to Housing Act.

It will help build more homes, limit investors from price-gouging housing, and cut red tape for manufactured homes.

posts.text:
The Senate voted to put a check on this administration’s war with Iran.

Right now, the administration is reportedly asking Congress for roughly $80 billion to cover the cost of the war.

This war should never have been started in the first place.

posts.text:
I voted yes on the ROAD to Housing Act to increase the number of homes and limit private equity from buying up single-family homes.

Americans should have a fair shot at buying and rehabbing a home without being priced out by out-of-state investors.

Now this heads to the House.

First the Reflecting Pool turned green with algae. Then the paint started peeling. Now it's headed for another round of repairs.

Another example of misplaced priorities when Americans are focused on the rising cost of everyday life.

posts.text:
I joined the Juneteenth celebration in Rondo to celebrate the end of slavery and honor a neighborhood whose history reflects both the challenges we've faced and the progress we've made.

With voting rights still under attack it is a reminder that the fight for justice never ends.
